Article Title: CBI secures deportation of fugitive wanted in Haryana murder case from Kazakhstan
Article Text:
Fugitive Ashish Kumar

CBI statement

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has secured the return of a man from Kazakhstan who was wanted in connection with a murder case in Haryana, the agency said on Wednesday.The operation was carried out in coordination with the ministry of external affairs, the ministry of home affairs and the Delhi Police.As per the agency, the accused, Ashish Kumar, was the subject of an Interpol Red Notice."The subject was wanted in connection with a murder case registered by the Haryana Police. The incident occurred in November 2025, when a dispute arose between the deceased and the subject during a marriage function. Subsequently, while the deceased was travelling from the venue, the subject, along with his associates, deliberately intercepted and stopped his vehicle midway and brutally assaulted him," the CBI said in a statement, adding that the assault resulted in fatal injuries to the victim.Kumar was traced to Almaty, Kazakhstan, following the publication of the Red Notice against him in September."At the request of Haryana Police, a Red Notice was published in September 2026 against the accused through INTERPOL channels. Subsequently, the subject was geo-located at Almaty (Kazakhstan) immigration. The subject arrived at New Delhi on 23.11.2026, where he was taken into custody by the officers of Haryana Police," the statement read.Through its Bharatpol portal, the CBI coordinates with law enforcement agencies across the country to facilitate international police cooperation.According to the agency, it has secured the return of more than 300 wanted criminals through Interpol channels since 2019, including 75 so far this year.
Article Summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has secured the return of a man from Kazakhstan. Ashish Kumar was wanted in connection with a murder case in Haryana. Kumar was traced to Almaty, Kazakhstan, following the publication of the Red Notice against him.

Article Title: 'Couldn't even fill single Ramlila Maidan': BJP's Nitin Nabin takes jibe at Rahul's 'vote chori' rally
Article Text:
Nitin Nabin hits out at Rahul Gandhi over 'vote chori' allegations

Nabin targets INDIA bloc over vote theft allegations

NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Monday targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his 'vote chori' allegations, claiming the INDIA bloc had failed to fill even a single Ramlila Maidan during its rally in Delhi. Addressing a BJP rally in Karimnagar, Telangana , Nabin said BJP workers had drawn larger crowds across more than 200 locations and accused Rahul of advocating for alleged infiltrators to be included in voter lists."Rahul Gandhi ji used to say that vote chori took place. Rahul ji, the people are with us, and the votes are with us. The people of Karimnagar have shown that their blessings are with us. They (the INDIA alliance), despite putting in their all, couldn't even fill a single Ramlila Maidan, while BJP workers gathered far more people than could fit in a Ramlila Maidan at over 200 locations," news agency ANI quoted him as saying.Nabin also questioned Rahul Gandhi's claim that 13 crore votes had been stolen and challenged his stand on the inclusion of people whose whereabouts were allegedly unverified."Rahul ji claimed that 13 crore people's votes had been stolen. But I would like to ask: Why should 3 crore people be included in the voter list? More than 6 crore people have shifted. I know that in Telangana, lakhs of people have shifted their votes.So, should people be allowed to vote twice? The remaining 3 crore are those whose whereabouts the Election Commission enquired about in 2003, but they have no answers. So, the person advocating for these 3 crore infiltrators is none other than Rahul Gandhi," he said.The BJP chief accused opposition parties of attempting to create chaos, while asserting that the BJP was receiving public support through democratic means."They tried to spread chaos—let them have their chaos! We, on the other hand, are receiving democracy's blessings," Nabin said.Taking a swipe at Rahul Gandhi's references to the Constitution, he said, "I have come to tell those who carry a copy of the Constitution around in their hands: you have a copy of the Constitution in your hands, but the Constitution is in our hearts. You speak of the Constitution, but we revere it. That is why we respect all constitutional institutions."He also invoked the Emergency to target the Congress, saying, "The people who murdered democracy by imposing the Emergency to save their own seats are today invoking democracy."Nabin also criticised Rahul Gandhi's remarks on India's economy, accusing him of insulting the country both within India and abroad."Whenever Rahul Gandhi is in the country, he does nothing but insult it, and he insults it abroad too. Rahul ji goes everywhere saying that India's economy is a disaster. Rahul ji, India's economy and its development are advancing on a global scale. Today, India has moved beyond the Fragile Five to become the world's fourth-largest economy," he said.Expressing confidence about the BJP's prospects in Telangana, Nabin said the party would hold the state government accountable."I am sure the countdown to the Telangana government has begun. BJP karyakartas will now hold the Telangana government accountable," he said.He also predicted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi would return to the Red Fort in 2029."Modi ji will not go anywhere; he will appear on the ramparts of the Red Fort again in 2029. Rahul ji, keep dreaming. India's youth, farmers, women, workers and people from every section of society stand with PM Modi. PM Modi is going nowhere. He will return to the ramparts of the Red Fort in 2029.Rahul ji, keep dreaming! The youth, farmers, women, workers and every section of Indian society stand with PM Modi," he said.Nabin's Telangana visit was part of the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajkata Hatao' campaign. The party has launched the campaign to counter what it describes as attempts by Congress and other opposition leaders, particularly Rahul Gandhi, to mislead people through fear, confusion and misinformation.
Article Summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin hits out at Rahul Gandhi over 'vote chori' allegations. Nabin claims INDIA bloc failed to fill even a single Ramlila Maidan during its rally in Delhi. Accuses Rahul of advocating for alleged infiltrators to be included in voter lists.

Article Title: 'Why remove mata Sita's name?' Congress slams BJP over 'Jai Shri Ram' remark
Article Text:
Congress slams BJP over 'Jai Shri Ram' remark

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Ajay Rai on Sunday criticised Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya over his remarks on the slogans 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Radhe Radhe', accusing the BJP leader of having a "perverted mindset" for dropping the name of Goddess Sita from the traditional greeting."This reflects the perverted mindset of Keshav Prasad Maurya. These are people with a perverted mindset. No one has any problem with the original phrasing. Previously, instead of 'Jai Shri Ram', the phrase used was 'Jai Siya Ram'—but these people have even removed the name of Mother Sita..." Rai said.His remarks came amid a war of words between Maurya and Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav over the BJP's slogan, 'Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De' (May the lotus bloom).On Sunday, Maurya took a swipe at the SP, saying its leaders had earlier felt uneasy hearing 'Jai Shri Ram' and were now troubled even by the chant of 'Radhe Radhe'.In a post on X, Maurya said, “SP leaders earlier felt uneasy hearing ‘Jai Shri Ram’. Now they are troubled even by ‘Radhe Radhe’.”“In Ayodhya, ‘Jai Shri Ram’ resonates, while in Braj people greet each other by saying ‘Radhe Radhe’,” he said.Asking Yadav to clarify his position, the deputy chief minister said, “Does this mean people in Uttar Pradesh will now have to seek his permission before taking the name of their deity?”Maurya accused the SP of indulging in appeasement politics and said both ‘Jai Shri Ram’ and ‘Radhe Radhe’ would continue to resonate in Uttar Pradesh.He also claimed that the party's hopes of returning to power in the 2027 Assembly elections would be dashed and that the BJP would form the government again.The exchange followed Yadav's remarks on Saturday, when he mocked the BJP's slogan during a press conference at the party headquarters in Lucknow.Referring to the slogan coined after the BJP's two-day meeting in Mathura, the former chief minister said the party was aware that its lotus symbol was wilting and was therefore chanting 'Radhe Radhe'.“‘Radhe Radhe’ is said at the time of farewell in our tradition. It means the BJP is going to be shown the door,” Yadav had said, claiming that the people of Uttar Pradesh would give the party a “grand farewell” in the coming elections.On Sunday, responding to Maurya's remarks, Yadav said, "I would never invite him to my house in my lifetime. But you (reporter) are welcome to visit our house; we will show you 'Radhe Radhe'.""'Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De' go ahead and make it bloom. Does it mean the lotus has withered? Why do you (BJP) need to make it bloom again? It has withered," he said at a press conference.Yadav also accused the BJP of selectively invoking religious sentiments, clarifying that his party was not opposed to 'katha' (religious discourses) but objected to controversial remarks about Hindu deities."The Samajwadi Party is not against 'katha'. But what were the views expressed about the father of Lord Shri Ram and what was said about our Lord Krishna? These are the same BJP people who once made Lord Hanuman dance at their programme," he said without naming anyone."Can you make such remarks about Lord Ram's father? Tell me, what would happen if someone among us made such a statement?" he added.
Article Summary: Congress leader Ajay Rai criticised Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya over his remarks on the slogans 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Radhe Radhe' Rai accused the BJP leader of having a "perverted mindset" for dropping the name of Goddess Sita from the traditional greeting. His remarks came amid a war of words between MauryA and Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav over the BJP's slogan.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) on Sunday launched a show, the “Cockroach Club”, aimed at engaging young people with the ideas of Mahatma Gandhi Jawaharlal Nehru and BR Ambedkar through discussions, cultural activities and live performances.The initiative comes as the CJP faces challenges in sustaining its street-level mobilisation amid legal hurdles and police action against its leaders. The group, which gained prominence through protests against examination irregularities and alleged voter roll manipulation, is now looking to create a space for young people to exchange ideas and engage in independent thinking.CJP leader Saurav Das announced the launch on X on Sunday, describing the Cockroach Club as a physical space where young people could come together to question, learn and exchange ideas.“The Cockroach Club will be a physical space for the young generation of this country. A place to come together, exchange ideas, question, learn, and grow. A space where young minds can engage with the ideas of Gandhi, Nehru, Ambedkar and other great thinkers through lectures and discussions,” Das wrote.He said the club would also organise film screenings and provide space for reading, studying and preparing for examinations.It would additionally host live performances and stand-up comedy, allowing young people to unwind and interact.“Above all, the Cockroach Club will be a space that encourages the young to think for themselves. But one where ideas are debated, perspectives challenged, and independent thought celebrated,” he added.The initiative marks an attempt by the group to maintain its connection with young people at a time when restrictions on protests have limited its ability to mobilise on the streets.The CJP first gained national attention through its protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar in June-July against the NEET paper leak and other examination-related irregularities. The agitation, according to the report, contributed to the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.However, subsequent protests over alleged Special Intensive Revision (SIR) irregularities and demands for action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar faced police action.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) on Sunday launched a show, the ‘Cockroach Club’ The club is aimed at engaging young people with the ideas of Mahatma Gandhi Jawaharlal Nehru and BR Ambedkar. The initiative comes as the CJP faces challenges in sustaining its street-level mobilisation.

Article Title: Bangladesh unrest: Bengal CM Suvendu to write to EAM, may push to extend minority entry cut-off
Article Text:
Adhikari indicated that the state could approach the Centre to extend this deadline for visa extension of religious minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who entered India by December 31, 2024 if the situation warranted it.

Suvendu cites protocol, says he cannot comment on foreign affairs

Suvendu flags possible extension of cut-off date

Bengal BJP chief calls for protests

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday said he would contact external affairs minister S Jaishankar on Monday to convey concerns in the state over the escalating violence in Bangladesh. He also indicated that the government could seek an extension of the cut-off date for religious minorities fleeing the neighbouring country to enter India.Suvendu said the developments in Bangladesh were "extremely painful" and had caused widespread concern in West Bengal, where many people have relatives across the border. He said the state government could also write to the Centre to seek an extension of the December 31, 2024 cut-off date for religious minorities entering India from Bangladesh, if required."Photographs and videos are coming in, and I am receiving phone calls. People are very worried. Around two crore people in Bengal have relatives there, and the developments are having an impact here as well. If required, we will write to the Centre to extend the timeline," he told reporters.The chief minister said he would speak to Jaishankar after his office opened on Monday and apprise him of the public reaction in West Bengal."As the chief minister of a state, I cannot comment directly on foreign affairs. There is a protocol. I will contact S Jaishankar after the office opens tomorrow and write to him, if required, to apprise him of the reaction here," he said.Suvendu said he had stood by the people of Bangladesh when he was in the Opposition. However, he said his position as the administrative head of a state placed certain limitations on what he could say or do."I also have some limitations. I cannot speak or act without restraint," he said.He did not specify how the unrest in Bangladesh had affected West Bengal.The chief minister's remarks come amid concerns over the safety of religious minorities in Bangladesh and the possibility of people fleeing to India.Under the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order, 2025, as amended in November 2026, religious minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who entered India by December 31, 2024, fleeing religious persecution, are exempt from entry-document requirements. However, they must obtain an appropriate visa to continue staying in the country.Suvendu indicated that the state could approach the Centre to extend this deadline if the situation warranted it.Meanwhile, West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya urged people to set aside political differences and organise protests against the violence in Bangladesh."As a Bengali Hindu, I appeal to everyone to rise above politics, build resistance and take to the streets. Protests should be held across the world because those being killed are our brothers," he said.Bhattacharya said the Centre would take appropriate decisions on the situation but maintained that people should raise their voices against the attacks.He also said he believed in the idea of "one nation" and argued that the Partition along religious lines had contributed to the present situation.The remarks come amid escalating political violence in Bangladesh, where supporters of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the banned Awami League clashed in several areas. The clashes prompted the deployment of hundreds of additional paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel.The developments came as Jamaat-e-Islami, the main parliamentary opposition party, launched a 40-day nationwide protest on Saturday. The protest coincided with the planned return of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina from India next month, despite her death sentence.
Article Summary: Suvendu Adhikari indicated that the state could approach the Centre to extend this deadline for visa extension of religious minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan. He said he would contact external affairs minister S Jaishankar on Monday to convey concerns in the state.

Article Title: Godhra train burning case: SC grants medical bail to convict after over 17 years in jail
Article Text:
Supreme Court grants medical bail to convict after 17 years in jail

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you feel about the handling of the 2002 Godhra train burning case over the years? It has been handled well. There have been serious flaws. I'm not sure. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday suspended the sentence of Irfan Siraj Pada, a convict in the 2002 Godhra train burning case , and granted him bail on medical grounds, taking note of his serious cardiovascular condition and more than 17 years in custody.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale passed the order after considering his medical condition, which the Gujarat government did not dispute, LiveLaw reported on Monday.According to legal news portal, the court took into account that Irfan suffers from a serious cardiovascular disease and has remained incarcerated for over 17 years. His appeal against the conviction is pending before the Supreme Court.The Godhra train burning took place on February 27, 2002, when 58 people were killed in a fire inside the S-6 coach of the Sabarmati Express, which was carrying kar sevaks returning from Ayodhya. The incident triggered communal riots across Gujarat.In March 2011, a trial court convicted 31 people in the case. Eleven were sentenced to death, while the remaining 20 were awarded life imprisonment. In 2017, the Gujarat high court commuted the death sentences of the 11 convicts to life terms and upheld the life sentences awarded to the other 20.Appeals against the convictions have been pending before the Supreme Court since 2018, LiveLaw reported.Irfan had also been granted interim parole in 2025 to allow the state government to consider his plea for premature release, according to the report.The latest order comes days after the Supreme Court suspended the life sentences of two other convicts in a separate case linked to the 2002 Gujarat riots . Last Tuesday, the court granted bail to Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya, who were convicted in the gangrape of Bilkis Bano and the murder of seven members of her family.In an order dated October 28, uploaded subsequently, a bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale noted that the two men had spent more than 17 years in prison and that one of them had a severe disability.“Having heard the parties, suffice it to state that the appellants have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years, and also the fact remains that one of the appellants has a severe handicap. Certainly, there are issues to be decided in the appeal, both on fact and law,” the bench said.“In view of the above and considering the issues involved in this appeal, we suspend the sentence and grant bail to the appellants on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the concerned trial court,” it added.
Article Summary: Supreme Court grants medical bail to convict after 17 years in jail. 58 people were killed in a fire inside the S-6 coach of the Sabarmati Express, which was carrying kar sevaks returning from Ayodhya. In March 2011, a trial court convicted 31 people in the case.

Article Title: Why clock starts ticking for cops as soon as a person is detained
Article Text:
Art 22(2) of the Constitution says an arrested person has to be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours.

Sunil Baghel

When does 24-hr period begin?

What SC said

Why 24-hr safegaurd matters

Can bail rules override rights?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

After police pick up a person, they have exactly 24 hours to produce them before a magistrate. SC has made it clear the deadline starts at the point of detention — not when the arrest is recorded — and exceeding it amounts to a violation of fundamental rights.explains. Supreme Court 's order on detention without prompt production before a magistrate speaks to one of the most fundamental rights - the right to freedom of movement. This is significant because this deadline has often been violated by delay in recording an arrest.The top court has clarified that only the time needed to travel from the place of arrest to the magistrate's court to produce a suspect can be excluded from the timeframe. Time spent in questioning, searches, seizures or other legal formalities must count towards the deadline.The court, in fact, also went a step further and clarified that sticking to the 24-hour window does not automatically make detention reasonable.In plain English, a suspect must not be held in custody unnecessarily just because police have 24 hours to produce him before a magistrate. They must justify every hour of curtailment of a suspect's freedom of movement and magistrates must examine how long a person was held and whether that period was justified.The Nov 5 order followed appeals by three men accused in a case involving the alleged transportation of over 60kg of contraband drugs in Tripura. A bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar held that their detention violated Art 22(2) of the Constitution and Sec 58 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 and set aside Tripura High Court's order rejecting their bail pleas.Customs officials had taken the men into custody on Sept 29, 2025 and their arrests were formally recorded the next morning. They were produced before a magistrate more than 24 hours after they were first detained (see box).Art 22(2) of the Constitution says an arrested person has to be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours. Detention beyond 24 hours requires a magistrate's authority. SC said the clock starts when a suspect is detained and their freedom is restricted, that is, "when his liberty is effectively curtailed".There is no constitutional basis, it said, for excluding time spent on investigation, interrogation, or legal formalities from the mandated 24 hours.The court also referred to Sec 58 of BNSS, which reflects the restriction in Sec 57 of the earlier Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), requiring detention to last no longer than is reasonable in the circumstances, even within the 24-hour limit.Additional solicitor general Raghavendra P Shankar, representing the Union govt, said the intervening hours before they were produced before a magistrate had been taken up by mandatory procedures like searches, seizures, preparing documents, questioning the accused, etc. He argued that arrest memos could be prepared only after the initial investigation. Until then, they were temporarily restrained to allow the search and seizure process to be completed.The govt relied on Rule 3(4) of NDPS Rules, 2022, which requires seized substances to be classified, weighed, packaged and numbered in the presence of search witnesses and the person from whom they were recovered. The govt argued that the time taken for these necessary steps could not be treated as detention following arrest.The bench examined earlier judgments on what amounts to arrest and custody, including a March 1980 SC judgment that held a person is in custody as soon as he is under the control of an investigating agency or an authority with powers to restrain him. Apart from citing these judgments in support of the accused, SC also rejected three HC decisions relied on by the govt, including Kannan vs State of Tamil Nadu (2026) that held that time spent on mandatory NDPS procedures before formal arrest could be excluded from the 24-hour calculation.SC instead said that search and seizure procedures did not prevent timely production before a magistrate. They could continue after production and authorisation of judicial custody.The judgment linked prompt production before a magistrate to protection against custodial violence. It cited a Dec 1980 SC judgment - against the backdrop of the Bhagalpur blinding incidents involving prisoners - that said the 24-hour requirement allowed judicial authorities to keep a check on police investigations.The bench also referred to the D K Basu case - that highlighted custodial violence and the practice of questioning suspects without formally recording their arrests, in which SC issued arrest safeguards in mid-90s. The latest judgment recalled earlier judicial concerns about people arrested without warrants being tortured to extract information, recover property or obtain confessions. It also cited an SC ruling in an Enforcement Directorate case, which held that a breach of Art 22(2) makes an arrest invalid and requires the court hearing the bail plea to release the accused.The court also examined Sec 37 of NDPS Act, which sets strict conditions for bail in cases involving commercial quantities of drugs. Tripura High Court had relied on an April 2026 ruling by a two-judge SC bench that held the two conditions under Sec 37 must be met before bail could be granted in such cases.The latest Supreme Court ruling questioned the suggestion that the right to a speedy trial under Art 21 must operate within the framework of Sec 37. It relied on the landmark Feb 2021 decision in Union of India vs KA Najeeb, where a three-judge SC bench recognised that strict provisions in special laws could not override fundamental rights under Art 21. It also made clear that NDPS procedures could not weaken the protection against unlawful detention under Art 22(2). In this case, the court found that the unexplained 18-hour gap between the end of search and seizure and the formal arrests was unreasonable under Sec 58 of BNSS, which states that "no police officer shall detain a person arrested without a warrant in custody for longer than is reasonable under the circumstances".
Article Summary: Art 22(2) of the Constitution says an arrested person has to be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours. The deadline has often been violated by delay in recording an arrest. Time spent in questioning, searches, seizures or other legal formalities must count towards the deadline.

Article Title: No bilateral talks with Pakistani minister on sidelines of SCO event: Culture secretary
Article Text:
The SCO forum saw cultural cooperation discussions among member nations, but no bilateral engagement with Pakistan's minister, the culture secretary said.

Indraprastha communique issued

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: No bilateral talks were held with Pakistan's minister on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, culture secretary Vivek Aggarwal said on Sunday. He said bilateral discussions took place with other participating countries during the three-day event, which concluded in the national capital.Pakistan's federal minister for climate change and environmental Coordination, Musadik Masood Malik, was among the delegates attending the forum. However, Aggarwal clarified that no bilateral meeting took place with the Pakistani minister.Aggarwal said the forum, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Purana Qila on November 20, saw discussions on strengthening civilisational ties and creating a roadmap for continued engagement among SCO countries."This has been a very successful event. It was called for by our Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Tianjin summit of SCO member countries. This event was inaugurated by our Prime Minister, and a lot of deliberations took place. Very positive discussions happened for the exchange of ideas, for the exchange of objects on civilisational narratives, on joint museum exhibitions, and on work regarding manuscripts and traditional knowledge systems," news agency ANI quoted him as saying.A formal Indraprastha communique was issued to outline the roadmap for continuing the dialogue, Aggarwal said."Overall, the outcome has been very, very pleasant. A formal Indraprastha communique has been issued on the discussions that have taken place to lay out a roadmap for the future of this civilizational dialogue to continue among the SCO countries," he added.Aggarwal said bilateral and minister-level discussions were held with participating countries on cultural exchange programmes and future cooperation."Lots of bilateral discussions took place with all the participating countries and minister-to-minister dialogues happened; Deputy Minister-to-Deputy Minister dialogues have happened and issues have been discussed on the cultural exchange programmes and on the future course of exchanges, which can be bilateral and multilateral," he said.The discussions also covered artist exchanges and people-to-people ties, he added.The three-day forum was organised following Modi's proposal at the 2025 SCO summit in Tianjin, China, to establish a dedicated platform for civilisational dialogue among member countries. The proposal was subsequently welcomed in the Bishkek Declaration.
Article Summary: SCO forum saw cultural cooperation discussions among member nations, but no bilateral engagement with Pakistan's minister. Culture secretary Vivek Aggarwal said bilateral discussions took place with other participating countries during the three-day event. A formal Indraprastha communique was issued to outline the roadmap for continuing the dialogue.

NEW DELHI: Russian President Vladimir Putin shared his fascination with ancient Indian culture and called Indian history stunning. He said, 'About 600 million.' And what's the total population of the country? About a billion. And the other two-thirds speak their own languages," Putin said.Reacting to the figures, the Russian president said, "Isn't that amazing? It's stunning!"He then cited India's civilisation as an example of the country's rich history and cultural heritage."Take, for example, Indian civilisation, the oldest one. It's very interesting. The more I learn about it, the more fascinated I become," Putin said.
Article Summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin shared his fascination with ancient Indian culture and called Indian history stunning. He described it as the oldest and called its linguistic diversity "stunning". Putin said he was increasingly fascinated by India's history and culture the more he learnt about them.

Article Title: Amit Shah inaugurates NDRF campus in Arunachal, stresses 'zero-casualty' disaster response
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah in Arunachal Pradesh.

Timely warnings help prevent casualties

Shah says migration has stopped in 40

border villages

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the government was following a 'zero-casualty' approach to disaster management, prioritising timely warnings and swift evacuations to protect people in vulnerable areas.Inaugurating the 12th battalion campus of the National Disaster Response Force ( NDRF ) at Hollongi near Itanagar, Shah said the facility would strengthen disaster preparedness and response across the Northeast, a region prone to natural calamities.He stressed the need for modern warning systems, better preparedness and coordinated efforts to minimise loss of life and property. The campus, he said, had been built to earthquake-resistant standards, keeping the region's seismic vulnerability in mind.Shah said expanding the NDRF, improving its resources and providing specialised training were key priorities for strengthening India's disaster management capabilities.Highlighting improvements in the country's disaster response system, Shah said cyclone warnings issued 24 to 48 hours in advance had helped authorities evacuate people from vulnerable areas and prevent casualties.He said several cyclones over the past four years had caused no loss of life, crediting improved forecasting, preparedness and coordinated evacuation efforts, PTI reported.The NDRF has carried out more than 11,000 rescue and relief operations in India and abroad, including in Japan, Nepal, Turkey and Sri Lanka, he said. Shah expressed confidence that the force would emerge as one of the world's leading disaster response agencies.He also underlined the importance of community participation, praising local volunteers, including scouts and trained 'Aapda Mitras', for assisting people during emergencies.He said disaster management should involve not just specialised forces but also grassroots workers and village-level functionaries.During his visit, Shah also highlighted development along Arunachal Pradesh's border with China, saying the population in 40 villages had increased and migration had stopped due to improvements in facilities and employment opportunities.Speaking at a cooperative conference, he said the Centre had directed the Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) to buy produce from local cooperatives in border villages instead of sourcing supplies from cities.“I reviewed this yesterday. I am pleased that people have begun returning to all 40 villages (bordering with China), the population there has increased, and migration has stopped. Electricity, employment, and health facilities have been discussed. Water has also been delivered to the hilltops. The home ministry has strictly mandated that the ITBP and the Army should not procure their produce from Tezpur or Guwahati; they must be procured from villages and cooperatives,” news agency ANI quoted Shah as saying.“Women in Arunachal Pradesh are supplying dairy products, eggs, vegetables, millets and flour through their cooperatives, bringing prosperity to rural households and transforming local agriculture and strengthening the relationship between villages and the army,” he added.Shah also urged cooperative institutions and women's self-help groups (SHGs) to work towards making the state self-reliant in essential food products.Shah launched 199 development projects worth Rs 110.95 crore under the Centre's Vibrant Villages Programme across 11 border districts of Arunachal Pradesh. He also unveiled the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047, a roadmap for the development of the cooperative sector.The home minister said the Centre would extend all necessary support to the state for its development. He added that Mobile Medical Units had been sent to villages in 11 border districts under the Vibrant Villages Programme.Shah also praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's decision to describe border villages as the country's 'first villages' rather than its last, saying they had a right to development.“Vibrant Village Programme was made for villages in border states. Earlier it was called the country's last village; Narendra Modi changed the concept and awarded the title of the first village in the country. The biggest right to development is of the border villages of the country,” he said.Earlier on Saturday, Shah chaired a high-level meeting in Itanagar to review law and order, internal security, border management and development in Arunachal Pradesh. He also reviewed border security and strategic infrastructure along the state's nearly 1,126-km international boundary with China.Shah congratulated the state government and people of Arunachal Pradesh on the establishment of the NDRF campus. He said the Northeast had an important role in India's development and security. The home minister later left for Delhi, concluding his three-day visit to the state.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the government was following a 'zero-casualty' approach to disaster management. He stressed the need for modern warning systems, better preparedness and coordinated efforts to minimise loss of life and property. Shah said cyclone warnings issued 24 to 48 hours in advance had helped authorities evacuate people from vulnerable areas.

Article Title: Kerala family gets Rs 5,218 water bill for 1.48 lakh litres despite claiming no usage, consumer commission cancels bill, orders KWA to test meter and pay Rs 25,000 compensation
Article Text:
(AI image) In Kerala, a family challenged a water bill of Rs 5,218 from the Kerala Water Authority.

KOTTAYAM: A family in Kerala received a water bill of Rs 5,218 for allegedly consuming 1.48 lakh litres over two months, despite claiming it had not used any water from the Kerala Water Authority (KWA) connection during the period.The district consumer disputes redressal commission has now cancelled the disputed bill, directed KWA to test the water meter and ordered it to pay the family Rs 20,000 as compensation and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.The commission also directed KWA to reassess the bill based on actual, legally ascertainable consumption and refund any excess amount collected. The authority has been given 30 days to comply, failing which interest will be applicable.The order was passed by a bench comprising commission president V S Manulal and members Bindu R and K M Anto on a complaint filed by Gigi Philip Vettithanam and Ancy G Philip, residents of S B High School Ward in Changanassery.According to the complaint, KWA had raised the bill for consumption of 1,48,000 litres between August and October 2025, although the family claimed it had not drawn any water from the connection during this period.The household primarily depends on its own well and uses the KWA supply only as a backup.The family pointed out that KWA's inspection report had recorded that the connection supplied only a 500-litre tank. Further, water meter readings between January 2022 and August 2025 showed consumption of just 2-5 kilolitres. The family had generally been paying the minimum bi-monthly charge of around Rs 145.On October 15, 2025, the complainants submitted three applications to KWA seeking cancellation of the disputed bill, temporary disconnection of the supply and technical testing of the meter. However, they alleged that the authority failed to act on their requests promptly.They also told the commission that access to KWA's online portal was blocked and that officials asked them to remove the government-owned meter themselves and bring it to the KWA office for testing. The family further alleged that it was asked to pay the disputed amount as a condition for temporary disconnection.Holding that KWA's actions amounted to deficiency in service, the commission directed the authority to cancel the bill, test the meter and issue a revised demand based on actual consumption. It also ordered a refund of any excess amount already collected.Philip, who studied consumer protection law and the rules governing KWA, argued the case himself."Government authorities are also accountable for the services they provide, and consumers have every right to seek legal remedies when those rights are violated," he said after the order.
Article Summary: A family in Kerala received a water bill of Rs 5,218 for allegedly consuming 1.48 lakh litres over two months. The family claimed it had not used any water from the Kerala Water Authority connection during the period. The district consumer disputes redressal commission has now cancelled the disputed bill, directed KWA to test the water meter and ordered it to pay the family.

Article Title: No safe waters for Russian ships? How Ukraine pulled off 2,400-km drone strike in Libya
Article Text:
How Ukraine managed to strike Russian warship thousands of kilometres from its coast

Why the destruction of Merkury is a major blow to Russia

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Russian ships are finding fewer safe waters as Ukraine takes its naval drone war far beyond the Black Sea, striking targets in the Mediterranean and Baltic Sea.In the latest blow, a Ukrainian drone attack set a Russian Navy corvette ablaze at a port in Libya, thousands of kilometres from the Ukrainian coastline.According to a report by The War Zone (TWZ), the attack took place on November 22 at Benghazi port in eastern Libya, where Ukrainian naval drones targeted the Russian Navy corvette Merkury and a Russian cargo vessel.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the operation on November 23, saying seven Ukrainian-made naval drones were used to sink the warship. Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) also claimed that a Russian Ka-27 military helicopter aboard the corvette was destroyed.Satellite imagery published by TWZ showed the vessel engulfed in flames before capsizing, with much of its hull subsequently submerged. The operation marked a significant escalation in Ukraine's efforts to strike Russian naval assets far beyond the immediate theatre of war.The Libya operation was not an isolated incident. Ukraine's naval drone campaign has increasingly extended to Russian vessels operating in other strategically important waterways, including the Baltic Sea.Just a day before the Benghazi attack, a Russian defence ministry-linked cargo ship, Sparta II, came under a suspected drone attack in the Gulf of Finland on November 21. The vessel was reportedly heading towards Russia's Kaliningrad exclave when it was struck and caught fire.Ukraine's ability to strike the Russian corvette Merkury in Libya, around 2,400 km from its front line, may be linked to its reported military presence in the North African country.According to the Ukrainian Security Service (SBU), seven domestically developed naval drones were transported to a designated location and launched from a so-called 'mothership'.The agency has not disclosed the vessel's identity, its departure point or the route taken by the drones. However, two Libyan military officials told the Associated Press (AP) that the drones were launched from a base operated by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, with at least four intercepted and two hitting the Russian warship.The reported Ukrainian presence in Libya dates back to an alleged military arrangement with the Tripoli-based government.French broadcaster Radio France Internationale (RFI), in an investigation published in April 2026, reported that more than 200 Ukrainian military officers and specialists were deployed at three locations in western Libya, citing two Libyan sources.These included an air force academy in Misrata, a facility near the Mellitah oil and gas complex in Zawiya, reportedly equipped to launch aerial and naval drones, and the headquarters of Libya's 111th Brigade near Tripoli.The sources said the deployment followed an alleged agreement in October 2025 under which Ukraine would train Libyan forces in drone warfare in exchange for establishing a military presence. Neither government publicly confirmed the arrangement.The reported military footprint has also been linked to previous Ukrainian operations against Russian vessels in the Mediterranean.RFI reported that the December 2025 attack on the Russian-linked tanker Qendil was launched from the Misrata area, while Ukrainian forces allegedly used a Magura V5 naval drone launched from the Mellitah facility to strike the Russian LNG carrier Arctic Metagaz in March 2026.Jalel Harchaoui, an analyst at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), told AP that the presence of Ukrainian operatives in the greater Tripoli area was "entirely plausible", suggesting it could have the knowledge and backing of Western powers.However, Kyiv has not publicly confirmed its military deployment in Libya, and the Tripoli government's defence ministry has denied allowing Libyan military facilities to be used for attacks against foreign countries.The loss of the Merkury is significant for Russia because the corvette was not only a combat vessel but also part of Moscow's maritime security network in the Mediterranean.According to Ukraine's Security Service (SBU), the warship regularly escorted Russian naval convoys, including the cargo ship MV Angara, which was used to transport military equipment along the so-called Syrian Express and Libyan Express supply routes.Commissioned in May 2023, the Merkury was among Russia's newer warships. The Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class corvette has a displacement of around 2,200 tonnes, measures 104.5 metres in length and can reach speeds of 27 knots.It has a crew of approximately 100 and carries eight Kh-35 anti-ship missiles, Redut air-defence missiles, a 100-mm naval gun and torpedoes. It can also operate a Ka-27 naval helicopter.Its reported role in escorting Russian military shipments made it a valuable asset beyond its direct combat capabilities. Its destruction could weaken Russia's ability to protect military cargo moving through the Mediterranean, while depriving its navy of a relatively new multi-role warship.
Article Summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the operation on November 23, saying seven Ukrainian-made naval drones were used to sink the warship. Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) also claimed that a Russian Ka-27 military helicopter aboard the corvette was destroyed.

Article Title: US spy chief confirms probe into Nvidia-linked chip supply network involving Alice Huang, China
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US spy chief Jay Clayton has confirmed that investigations into Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed, are ongoing amid the controversy surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The confirmation comes after reports suggesting Alice Huang remained in contact with an official from China's ministry of state security for more than a year.The probes are linked to allegations that the company was part of a network involved in supplying Nvidia-powered servers to Chinese customers.In an interview with Fox News, Clayton said investigations into both Huang and the company were progressing alongside regulatory proceedings. He also indicated that Nvidia's board of directors was expected to examine the matter."There is an investigation into her company, and there is an investigation into her. That is going to play out," Clayton said."Also, I fully expect that the board of directors of Nvidia is looking into this situation. You know, that would be responsible; that's what the American people want to hear from them. And there are—are regulatory proceedings going on.The American people will get answers regarding this matter," he added.The investigations come amid controversy surrounding former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang, who resigned on November 12 following reports of an alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by US intelligence agencies of having links to Chinese intelligence.Jensen Huang had acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife. Nvidia, however, said it had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets had been compromised.Nvidia board chairman Harvey Jones said directors had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him. Chief financial officer Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO. Huang had said he would be honoured to return if the board considered it in the company's interest.This comes after a Wall Street Journal (WSJ) report, published on Saturday, detailed the alleged role of Chinese national Li Ming in a network of companies supplying computing capacity to Chinese customers through Southeast Asia.According to the report, Li, 52, was closely involved in Megaspeed's operations and major business decisions. Singapore prosecutors charged him and others with fraud in February 2025 over the alleged transshipment of servers containing Nvidia chips. Megaspeed was not named in those charges.The WSJ reported that Li worked with Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, and that the three helped establish a network of partners across Southeast Asia. Megaspeed subsequently joined Nvidia's cloud partner programme in November 2023, gaining priority access to its latest chips, the newspaper reported.The report also alleged that some servers were transferred to Shanghai-based Century Litong in violation of US export controls. Nvidia placed Megaspeed on an internal "no sell" list in June 2025.Megaspeed has maintained that its business was legitimate and lawful, adding that Alice Huang left in August 2025. Singapore authorities reportedly questioned her over suspected chip smuggling and barred her from re-entering the country.The WSJ further reported that a new venture, Novagate Cloud, had received at least $300 million worth of Nvidia-chip hardware in Malaysia during the first five months of 2026.Meanwhile, The New York Times reported on Sunday that Alice Huang remained in contact with an official from China's state security ministry for more than a year, from spring 2025 to autumn 2026, during her alleged affair with Jensen Huang.The report further said that US intelligence agencies had gathered evidence suggesting that Alice's business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, had also worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. The extent and timing of both individuals' alleged contacts with the agency had not been previously reported, the newspaper said.
Article Summary: US spy chief Jay Clayton confirms investigations into Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed. Comes after reports suggesting Alice Huang remained in contact with an official from China's ministry of state security for more than a year. probes are linked to allegations that the company was part of a network involved in supplying Nvidia-powered servers to Chinese customers.

Article Title: Adani power project in Satara: ‘Nod covers 4 villages, excavation on at 5th’
Article Text:
Adani Green Energy Ltd's Tarali pumped storage project is under investigation due to alleged unauthorized work at Sawarghar.





MUMBAI: Amid a row over work on Adani Green Energy Ltd’s (AGEL) 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project beginning in Satara’s Patan taluka despite lack of approval from National Board for Wildlife (NBWL), the state forest department’s honorary wildlife warden for the district has written to Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) alleging that large-scale excavation and construction is underway in Sawarghar village, which was not listed on the environmental clearance (EC) granted by the Union forest ministry on Feb 11 last year.The honorary wildlife warden, Rohan Bhate, said the EC specified only four villages that stand to be affected—Nivade, Tondoshi, Kalambe and Jalu—in the district.A spokesperson from Adani Group said the EC covers the four villages as well as Dafalwadi, and the company later purchased private land in Sawarghar to set up temporary accommodation for workers. The company said such an accommodation was included in the project layout approval from Central Electricity Authority. It said the project has all the relevant clearances and initial works are in progress at the site.The Tarali project, estimated at Rs 5,675 crore, is planned over 150.7 hectares of private land.In his letter to MPCB member-secretary Rahul Rekhawar, Bhate claimed that the activity in Sawarghar did not have the required EC and NBWL’s approval, and sought urgent intervention and an independent investigation.Rekhawar confirmed that MPCB has received Bhate’s letter and said it is investigating the allegations.Amol Satpute, MPCB sub-regional officer in Satara, said a team from the pollution regulator inspected the Sawarghar site on Friday, where excavation was underway. Satpute said when officials questioned the site supervisor, they were told the developer was levelling land to set up a labour camp for the Tarali project. He said a report would be submitted to higher authorities.Bhate said the situation raised questions about the geographical scope and validity of the EC in relation to the work being carried out at Sawarghar. He questioned whether MPCB had verified that the proponent had obtained environmental and wildlife clearances for all land parcels involved before issuing the mandatory ‘consent to establish’ (CTE) that allows construction to begin. He said MPCB cannot distance itself from responsibility because the CTE stage is a crucial regulatory checkpoint.Bhate requested an immediate site inspection and preparation of an official panchnama by MPCB officials to document the extent of excavation and construction, the machinery deployed, and the exact location of the work. He said if any excavation or construction is found to have started without statutory approvals, authorities should register the appropriate offence and initiate legal proceedings against responsible individuals and project authorities.He also asked MPCB to determine whether activity at Sawarghar is covered by the Feb 11, 2025, EC and whether all applicable environmental permissions for that specific location have been obtained. In addition, he sought verification of whether prior approval from the NBWL’s standing committee was secured wherever legally required.Bhate said the proposed project falls within the deemed eco-sensitive zone of Koyna wildlife sanctuary and the Sahyadri tiger reserve, making strict scrutiny under environmental and wildlife protection provisions essential. He requested that the matter be assigned to an impartial higher-level authority for an independent inquiry rather than being examined only by officials linked to project clearances. Pending verification, he asked for directions to prevent any further unauthorised excavation or construction at the site.Sources said AGEL has not yet complied with the stop-work order issued on Nov 13 by Satpute, in his capacity as the Satara division’s deputy conservator of forests, for starting work on the project without NBWL’s approval. Adani Group had earlier said the proposal had been submitted to NBWL. Satpute said he would need to check whether the developer had followed the order.
Article Summary: Adani Green Energy Ltd’s 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project is under investigation due to alleged unauthorized work at Sawarghar. Forest department's honorary wildlife warden has written to Maharashtra Pollution Control Board alleging that large-scale excavation and construction is underway.

Article Title: Buffs break away from fight, charge at 8-year-old boy, trample him to death in Ujjain
Article Text:
Eight-year-old boy named Yuvraj was killed by charging buffaloes during a traditional fight in Ujjain.





UJJAIN: In a tragic turn of events, an eight-year-old boy was trampled to death by charging buffaloes while watching a buffalo fight with his father on Friday. The incident took place at Hamukhedi on Dewas Road, in the Nagjhiri police station area of Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain district.The buffalo fight, it turns out, is a traditional event held on the occasion of Dev Prabodhini Ekadashi, a calendar festival.The bout between two buffaloes was being staged in a field near the govt school. Around 2 pm, Akash arrived with his son Yuvraj to catch the fight. He stood at the edge of the crowd, while the boy sat close to him, eating poha (a popular local snack).As the buffaloes, released from their pen or enclosure, charged towards the spectators, one climbed onto Yuvraj’s chest. His father jumped to his rescue, and was joined by some bystanders who eventually helped pull the child out from under the marauding feet of the buffs.The boy was rushed to a hospital where the doctors declared him dead on arrival.Akash, a taxi driver, said Yuvraj, a Class 3 student, was his only son. “The buffaloes were in a fight and had locked horns. My son was sitting close to me as we watched the fight. However, all of a sudden, the buffaloes came charging in our direction and trampled my child,” the father said, laying the blame on the organiser.A private hospital in Chandesari declared him dead on arrival, after which his body was taken to the district hospital at Charak Bhawan, where a post-mortem was conducted before the last remains were handed to the family.Nagjhiri station in-charge Rakesh Bharti said such events are illegal, adding that the incident was being investigated. He said the organiser had been warned two days earlier and had promised not to hold the event, yet went ahead with it.A case of unnatural death was registered, the officer said, adding that a criminal case will be filed against the accused once the inquiry establishes the facts. Statements from the family are yet to be recorded.Local residents said a similar event three to four years ago had led to stone pelting at the police.
Article Summary: Eight-year-old trampled to death by charging buffaloes during a traditional fight in Ujjain. Incident took place at Hamukhedi on Dewas Road, in the Nagjhiri police station area of Madhya Pradesh’s UJJain district.

Article Title: Rajasthan couple murdered by relative over vacating rented room
Article Text:
Couple killed by a distant relative following their request for him to leave his rental space





RAJKOT: A couple were killed and two of their relatives seriously injured when a distant relative of theirs attacked them with a nail-studded wooden club, as he held a grudge about being given notice to vacate the room they had rented to him, in Jangvad village of Jasdan taluka on Thursday.According to the FIR registered at Atkot police station on Friday, the deceased are Vilas Ghodakiya (32) and her husband, Prakash (35). The injured include the complainant, Labhu Ghodakiya (35), Prakash’s sister-in-law, and Puri, the wife of Labhu’s nephew.Atkot police arrested the accused, Ashok Ghodakiya, a resident of the same village, on charges of murder.Talking to TOI, Jasdan assistant superintendent of police Naveen Chakravarthy Repudi said the accused was unemployed and had been given a room to stay by the victims. “When they asked him to vacate the room, he held a grudge about it. He later attacked them with a club which had nails in it, which caused grievous head injuries to the victims,” he said.According to Labhu’s complaint, around 3.30pm on Thursday, she had gone to Prakash’s house to bring back her young son, Vraj, There was a knock on the door and when. Vilas opened it they and saw Ashok — a distant cousin of Prakash’s — carrying a wooden club.He began hurling abuses.When Labhu and Vilas objected to his language, Ashok allegedly threatened to kill them and swung the club at Labhu’s head. She suffered an injury to her left palm while trying to block the first blow, before a second strike hit the left side of her head.When Vilas intervened to save Labhu, Ashok struck her repeatedly on the head with the club. Hearing their screams, Prakash rushed out, followed by Puri, who was sitting at a kirana shop behind the house. Both were allegedly hit on their heads until they collapsed.The accused fled after Labhu’s eldest brother-in-law, Ramesh, arrived. The two injured victims are getting treatment at a hospital.
Article Summary: Vilas Ghodakiya (32) and her husband, Prakash (35), were killed in Jangvad village of Jasdan taluka on Thursday. The injured include the complainant, Labhu Ghodkiya (35) and Puri, the wife of Labhu’s nephew. Atkot police arrested the accused, Ashok Godakiya, on charges of murder.

Article Title: Bihar horror: Student dragged, molested; male friend assaulted, 3 arrested after video surfaces
Article Text:
Muzaffarpur district witnessed a rapid police response as three men were arrested within 12 hours for the alleged molestation of a student





PATNA: Police arrested three men within 12 hours of an incident in which a student was allegedly molested, assaulted and verbally abused in the Bochahan police station area of Muzaffarpur district.A video of the incident reportedly circulated on social media, prompting police to launch an investigation and identify the accused.The arrested men were identified as Anurag Kumar, son of Shivnath Sharma and a resident of Ward No. 1 in Kashirampur village; Vishal Kumar, son of Ram Kumar Sharma; and Ujjwal Kumar, son of Lal Babu Rai, a resident of Bhorhan village. All three were taken to Bochahan police station for questioning before being formally booked in the case.Alay Vats, Sub-Divisional Police Officer (East-I), said the incident came to light on November 19 after the video surfaced on social media."In the video, the accused molested the girl and indulged in indecent behaviour, while her friend was assaulted. Taking the matter seriously, officers began verifying the footage, examined the circumstances of the incident and identified those involved. Following the investigation and verification of the location, a police team conducted raids and apprehended all three accused within 12 hours," he said.Police also seized two mobile phones allegedly used to record and circulate the video. An FIR was registered under relevant sections of the law, and the process of sending the arrested men to judicial custody was initiated.Bochahan SHO Yashwant Kumar Mishra said police acted immediately after receiving information about the incident and intensified efforts to identify and arrest the accused. He confirmed that three men had been arrested, two mobile phones seized and further investigation was under way.The arrests were made by a team from Bochahan police station under the supervision of SDPO East-I, with the SHO leading the operation.
Article Summary: Muzaffarpur district witnessed a rapid police response as three men were arrested within 12 hours for the alleged molestation of a student. A video of the incident reportedly circulated on social media, prompting police to launch an investigation and identify the accused. The arrested men were identified as Anurag Kumar, Vishal Kumar and Ujjwal Kumar.

PIMPRI CHINCHWAD: Shiv Sena (UBT) has announced a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC, escalating the political row over an incident involving a photograph of party founder Balasaheb Thackeray.Making the announcement on Thursday, Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Pimpri Chinchwad unit president Chetan Pawar told reporters that the reward was being offered in response to a similar announcement by a Shiv Sena (UBT) office-bearer from Mumbai."As everyone knows, our party office-bearer from Mumbai has already announced a reward of Rs 1 lakh for anyone who slaps Shaina NC. Similarly, we, as the Pimpri Chinchwad unit of Shiv Sena (UBT), announce a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps her," Pawar said.The controversy erupted on Wednesday during a press conference organised by the Shinde-led Shiv Sena in Mumbai to protest against references to Hindutva ideologue V D Savarkar in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love.During the protest, party leaders tore pages from the book. Shaina was also seen tearing a portion of a photograph depicting Balasaheb Thackeray striking an effigy of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar with a slipper.The incident was captured on camera and drew criticism from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Shaina denied deliberately disrespecting Balasaheb, maintaining that she had torn the portion showing Aiyar and not the photograph of the late Shiv Sena founder. Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also defended her explanation.On Thursday, Shaina apologised to Balasaheb's admirers if her actions had hurt their sentiments, while insisting that she had no intention of disrespecting him.The incident has triggered a fresh confrontation between the rival Shiv Sena factions led by Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) has offered a reward in response to similar announcements made by rival factions. Row over Balasaheb Thackeray's photograph has triggered a fresh confrontation between the rival Shiv Sena factions led by Uddhav Thackersay and Eknath Shinde.

Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.

Article Title: As US gets ready to celebrate Thanksgiving, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton sends a 'warning'; says: American people should be ...
Article Text:
Trump has named intelligence chief Jay Clayton as his AI czar, putting him in charge of a new White House task force that will examine AI’s risks and opportunities and recommend how the US government should respond.

Americans should be prepared for disruptions

What happened
