Treasury secretary compares upgrades to a vaccine

As the Americans can preparing to travel for Thanksgiving, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that the disruptions in technology may continue as companies and government agencies are modernising their systems for the age of artificial intelligence. Appearing on CNN’s “State of the Union,” Clayton said outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI era. He said the public should expect heavy investment in upgrading systems and in cybersecurity, and that any major leap in technology, in computing power or applications, brings disruption. People should understand that systems will be upgraded and may be interrupted for a time, he said, and that companies and the government are dealing with the problem proactively.Speaking on CNN's State of the Union, Clayton said the public should expect temporary interruptions as organisations invest heavily in new technologies and cybersecurity measures. "The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton said, according to a CNBC report.He added that people should understand that system upgrades may occasionally result in service interruptions while both government agencies and private companies work to strengthen infrastructure and security. "You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot," he said.Government officials have largely dismissed the idea that the outages are linked to a coordinated cyberattack or one driven by artificial intelligence. The disruptions also slowed some bank transactions.A technology failure triggered a nationwide ground stop for flights just over a week ago that lasted for hours. The Federal Aviation Administration said router upgrades produced a flood of data that caused the stoppage, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack. Microsoft separately said its Outlook outage resulted from an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message during an appearance on CBS' Face the Nation, urging Americans not to worry about the security of their financial institutions. Asked whether consumers should be concerned about banks, Bessent replied, "No, they shouldn't."Referring to software updates and security improvements designed to protect systems against emerging AI-related threats, he acknowledged that occasional glitches may occur."The patches may cause a glitch," Bessent said. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency."
Article Summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton says companies and government are upgrading systems for the age of artificial intelligence. Clayton said the public should expect temporary interruptions as organisations invest heavily in new technologies and cybersecurity measures. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Americans not to worry about their financial institutions.

Article Title: Delhi cop suspended after calling off wedding over Maruti Brezza dowry demand in Haryana
Article Text:
Kuldeep (L), who is posted in the Delhi Police's Outernorth District, has been placed under suspension pending departmental action.

(With inputs from PTI)





SONIPAT: A Delhi Police constable has been suspended with immediate effect over allegations that he demanded dowry and called off his wedding after the bride's family failed to arrange a Maruti Brezza of his choice, an official said on Monday.Constable Kuldeep, who is posted in the Delhi Police's Outernorth District, has been placed under suspension pending departmental action."Taking serious note of the allegations regarding the demand for dowry and the subsequent calling off of the marriage, the misconduct of Constable Kuldeep has been viewed seriously. Accordingly, he has been placed under suspension with immediate effect, pending departmental action. The incident pertains to Sonepat in Haryana," statement of the Delhi Police read.The statement further said the conduct of the police personnel had been viewed with utmost seriousness and necessary departmental proceedings had been initiated against him as per the prescribed rules.The incident took place on November 20 in Sonipat, Haryana, where the wedding was scheduled to be held at Mamchand Vatika.In his complaint, the bride's father, Subhash Kumar, said he had booked a Hyundai Aura worth around Rs 9.5 lakh for the groom.However, Kuldeep allegedly insisted on a Maruti Brezza costing around Rs 13 lakh, saying he did not like the car booked for him.Kumar claimed he cancelled the Hyundai Aura booking and tried to arrange a Brezza but could not find one as it was unavailable at some showrooms.The bride's family also alleged that they had arranged furniture, including sofas and an almirah, a two-tola gold chain for the groom and four-tola gold earrings for his mother, along with other gifts.The complainant further alleged that the groom's family demanded jewellery for the groom's brother and his wife. At the family's insistence, they had also arranged a decorated mare and a DJ for the wedding.On the wedding day, Kuldeep and his mother allegedly reached the venue in ordinary clothes at around 7.15 pm. After discovering that the Brezza had not been arranged, he allegedly abused the bride's family and left with his mother despite repeated requests to complete the wedding rituals.Sonipat deputy commissioner of police Jitender Gahlawat said on Monday that a complaint had been received from the bride's family.Police said the family had sought a day's time to try to settle the matter through community members and requested that no action be taken until then.
Article Summary: Constable Kuldeep, who is posted in the Delhi Police's Outernorth District, has been placed under suspension pending departmental action. The incident took place on November 20 in Sonipat, Haryana. The bride's father, Subhash Kumar, said he had booked a Hyundai Aura worth around Rs 9.5 lakh for the groom.

Article Title: Contract appointees cannot be removed arbitrarily before tenure ends, says Karnataka HC
Article Text:
Justice S Sunil Dutt Yadav

set aside the state govt’s order replacing Puttaswamy with

IFS officer

BR Ramesh

. The court directed that Puttaswamy be reinstated forthwith, and in any event within a week from November 20, when the order was passed.





Bengaluru: Contractual appointment does not mean an employee can be removed at will before the agreed tenure ends, Karnataka High Court has held while ordering the reinstatement of CT Puttaswamy, Director (Technical Cell) in the Department of Forest, Ecology and Environment.The court also directed govt to pay him his salary from the date of the impugned order and permitted him to continue in the post on the same terms until the end of his tenure on January 27, 2027.Puttaswamy, who was earlier a professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering, had been appointed on contract as Director (Technical Cell) for one year from January 27, 2025, “or until further orders”. His tenure was extended by another year from January 27, 2026. However, on July 24, 2026, govt replaced him with Ramesh with immediate effect.Govt contended that the appointment was only “until further orders” and that a person on deputation has no indefeasible right to continue in a borrowed post.Rejecting the argument, the court noted that the order extending Puttaswamy’s tenure had expressly stated that his contractual appointment was being extended for one year from January 27, 2026.The court also drew a distinction between ordinary deputation and Puttaswamy’s appointment.Puttaswamy was working at BMS Engineering College, a private institution, and had entered govt service through the rules permitting lateral appointment to a senior post. This, the court said, gave his appointment “further qualitative protection”, as it was a deputation by appointment and not merely a deputation by transfer.“While a deputationist may not normally have an indefeasible right to continue, though law does extend protection against arbitrariness, the posting of the petitioner as described above would confer further qualitative protection by virtue of it being a deputation by appointment and not a deputation by transfer,” the court observed. It further said that Puttaswamy had been displaced contemporaneously with the appointment of his replacement, but the govt order did not provide any reason for his removal. The absence of reasons, the court held, rendered the govt’s action “arbitrary or capricious”. The court, however, rejected Puttaswamy’s plea seeking continuation in service until January 26, 2028.
Article Summary: Karnataka High Court orders reinstatement of CT Puttaswamy, Director (Technical Cell) in Department of Forest, Ecology and Environment. The court also directed govt to pay him his salary from the date of the impugned order and permitted him to continue in the post.

Article Title: HC rejects accident victim’s appeal, cites inconsistencies in evidence
Article Text: Bengaluru: Pointing out at least four discrepancies in the accident victim’s version of events, Karnataka High Court has dismissed his appeal challenging a tribunal order that rejected his claim for compensation over injuries sustained in a 2015 road accident. Justice KB Geetha, in an order dated Nov 6, observed that inconsistencies in the claimant’s account, including discrepancies in the identity of a prosecution witness, the location and circumstances of the accident, and the treatment history, raised serious doubts about his version of events.The first discrepancy concerned the name and father’s name of one of the prosecution witnesses. The details differed across the affidavit evidence, cross-examination, supporting documents and charge sheet. The court said it was difficult to accept that prosecution witness No. 3 was the same person as charge-sheet witness No. 2. Secondly, the place of the accident was mentioned differently in various documents. Thirdly, the history of the accident recorded at govt Wenlock District Hospital and KMC Hospital was inconsistent. Fourthly, although the claimant maintained that he was initially taken to AJ Hospital and Research Centre, its records contained no material to establish that he had received even outpatient treatment there.The appellant, Santhosh Kumar , a resident of Mangaluru taluk in Dakshina Kannada district, had approached Motor Accident Claims Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for injuries sustained in an accident on Sept 16, 2015, at around 9.30 pm. The accident allegedly occurred in front of the Bata showroom near the KSRTC Bijai bus stand in Mangaluru.According to his claim, he was travelling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle driven by Raghavendra when a car hit the two-wheeler, leaving him injured. He claimed that he was taken to govt Wenlock District Hospital, where he was admitted from Sept 17 to Oct 5, 2015. He also claimed to have incurred Rs 30,000 in medical and miscellaneous expenses and sought another Rs 30,000 towards future medical expenses.The claimant further submitted that he was a final-year mechanical engineering student at Shrinivasa College, Valachhil, and earned Rs 6,000 per month by conducting tuition classes. The tribunal dismissed his compensation claim on Feb 16, 2023, following which he approached the High Court. On examining the records, Justice Geetha noted that while the claimant placed the accident at Bijai at 9.30 pm, the discharge summary and inpatient case sheet of Wenlock Hospital recorded the location as near Nanthoor and the time as 8.45 pm.The court also referred to his subsequent treatment at KMC Hospital from April 7 to 12, 2016, around six months after the alleged accident. The hospital records described the earlier incident as a bike skid and fall, following which he was treated at Wenlock Hospital for a right femur shaft fracture and underwent fracture fixation with nailing. The records also stated that he had no history of fresh trauma or injury.Further, the court noted that the motorcycle rider Raghavendra’s father’s name appeared as Mahaveer, Mahaveer Gowda and MI Hire Gowda in different records. Citing these inconsistencies, the High Court dismissed Santhosh Kumar’s appeal.
Article Summary: Karnataka High Court has dismissed his appeal challenging a tribunal order that rejected his claim for compensation over injuries sustained in a 2015 road accident. Justice KB Geetha, in an order dated Nov 6, observed that inconsistencies in the claimant’s account raised serious doubts about his version of events.

Article Title: AKU team develops 2 new materials for LED devices
Article Text:
Aryabhatta Knowledge University

Patna

:

Discover Materials





Researchers at Aryabhatta Knowledge University (AKU), Patna, have developed two materials that produce blue light when exposed to ultraviolet rays, a finding that could help further research into materials used in LED lights and other light-based electronic devices.The researchers at AKU’s Nanoscience and Nanotechnology Centre developed the two materials, samarium iron garnet and gadolinium iron garnet, using a low-cost chemical process. During laboratory tests, both materials emitted blue light when exposed to ultraviolet radiation at a wavelength of 200 nanometres. The researchers also studied their electrical, optical and magnetic properties.According to Rakesh Kumar Singh, head of the centre, the findings could pave the way for further research into the possible use of these materials in devices that produce or respond to light. He said the research was carried out as part of MTech researcher Amit Kumar’s work under his supervision. The team also included Nishant Kumar, Abhay Kumar Aman, Bibhuti Vikramaditya and Kamesh Kumar, former registrar of Maulana Mazharul Haque Arabic and Persian University, Patna.The paper was published in Springer Nature’son Aug 12, 2025. Its abstract has also been indexed in Science Explorer (SciX), a multidisciplinary digital library operated by the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory under an agreement with NASA. SciX is built on the Astrophysics Data System based at the Center for Astrophysics at Harvard.
Article Summary: Researchers at Aryabhatta Knowledge University (AKU), Patna, have developed two materials that produce blue light when exposed to ultraviolet rays. The finding could help further research into materials used in LED lights and other light- based electronic devices.

Article Title: US army seeks to proceed with 5-tonne chemical blast in Iowa despite court order halting detonation
Article Text:
US Army seeks to proceed with Iowa chemical blast despite court order halting detonation.

Why the Army wants to proceed with the explosion

Residents fear lead contamination, health risks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The US Army is seeking to bypass a federal court order blocking its plan to detonate five tonnes of potentially dangerous explosive chemicals in Iowa, arguing that delaying the operation could increase the risk of an accidental explosion as temperatures drop.Government lawyers urged the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals to allow the Army to proceed with the operation, saying swift action was necessary to protect military personnel and nearby communities, according to an Associated Press report."Protection of human health and the environment demand action now, not delay," the government lawyers said in a court filing late Saturday, adding that the Army wanted to carry out the detonation by Tuesday.The planned operation involves destroying 68 drums containing around five tonnes of lead azide, an explosive chemical used in the manufacture of munitions. The material was discovered in a deteriorating condition at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in March.A federal appeals court had earlier put the operation on hold after environmental groups challenged an emergency permit issued by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).The detonation was initially scheduled for Friday but was postponed to Monday following concerns raised by residents and elected officials.Army officials have argued that the lead azide has become extremely unstable because of its deteriorating condition and could explode accidentally if handled or transported.According to officials, crystallisation of the chemical inside the drums has increased the risk of an uncontrolled explosion. They have warned that even slight friction or movement could trigger a blast, making relocation or alternative disposal methods potentially dangerous.Government lawyers also argued that falling temperatures could further destabilise the material, increasing the threat of an accidental explosion. They said temperatures in the region were expected to drop below 30 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 1 degree Celsius) in the coming days.The Army has maintained that a controlled detonation is the safest available option after consulting explosives experts, engineers and environmental safety specialists.However, environmental groups have questioned whether all possible alternatives were properly examined. They have also criticised authorities for failing to provide sufficient information to residents who could be affected by the operation.The proposed explosion has triggered concerns among residents in and around Middletown, a small community in southeastern Iowa located about 160 miles from Des Moines.The Army has acknowledged that the detonation could release lead-containing particles into the air, forming a plume that could eventually settle on the ground.Lead exposure can cause serious health problems, and there is no known safe level of lead exposure. Residents have expressed concerns about possible contamination of farmland, crops, livestock, pets and nearby properties.Some residents have also been warned about potential damage to windows due to the noise and ground vibrations caused by the explosion.The Army had recommended that people in affected areas remain indoors, keep doors and windows closed, bring pets and livestock inside and clean outdoor surfaces after the operation. Residents were also advised to take precautions to prevent contaminated dust from entering their homes.Environmental groups, including the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club, have called for greater transparency and a review of the emergency permit granted by the EPA.They argue that communities deserve more advance notice and clearer information about the possible consequences of the explosion.
Article Summary: US Army seeks to bypass a federal court order blocking its plan to detonate five tonnes of potentially dangerous explosive chemicals in Iowa. Government lawyers urged the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals to allow the Army to proceed with the operation. They argued that delaying the operation could increase the risk of an accidental explosion as temperatures drop. Environmental groups have challenged an emergency permit issued by the EPA.

Article Title: ​Police’s own photos expose wrong e-challans issued to same family in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
File photo

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Two separate incidents in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar have exposed acts of wrongful challans issued by the traffic police against members of the same family.In the first e-challan, the traffic police fined the wrong vehicle due to a wrong letter in the car number. In the other case, the police first fined a car driver for not wearing a helmet and then issued the same challan for overspeeding, even though the police speed camera showed the car was within limits.In both cases, the police’s own photographs contradict their challans, yet both fines still stand against two members of the same family from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The first case is of a car, MH20-EY0545. An e-challan was issued against the car’s owner on Saturday for using a mobile phone while driving. However, the photograph attached as proof shows a completely different vehicle — MH20-EA0545. The difference is of one letter — Y in place of A — in the number of both cars.“I was shocked to see a message on my mobile about a traffic violation when I had not even driven the car on Saturday,” said Nityanand Zadbuke, the car owner.The second incident involved Nityanand’s elder brother, Dr Amol Zadbuke, a health professional.The owner of car number MH20-CH3609 had first received an e-challan for not wearing a helmet in Dec last year. “I was taken aback by the traffic violation. When I raised a dispute, the same challan issued last year was shown as proof of overspeeding. But police’s own speed-camera photo shows my vehicle was moving at 57 Km/hr, which is well within the permissible speed of 95 Km/ hr,” Dr Zadbuke said.When contacted, Subhash Bhujang, the assistant commissioner of police (traffic), said that complaints related to both e-challans would be examined if vehicle owners approach the traffic police.“Misreading of letters on a number plate by the technical system cannot be ruled out, as vehicles are constantly moving. The other case with Dr Zadbuke is exceptional, and official intervention will be offered if the vehicle owner is not happy with the earlier grievance redressal,” he said.
Article Summary: In the first e-challan, the traffic police fined the wrong vehicle due to a wrong letter in the car number. In the other case, the police first fined a car driver for not wearing a helmet and then issued same challan for overspeeding.

Article Title: Delhi Police registers FIR against organisers for holding 2,000-person running event at JLN Stadium despite denial of permission
Article Text:
Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in New Delhi.





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has registered an FIR against the organisers of a large-scale running event held at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on October 11, allegedly in violation of a police order denying permission for the gathering.According to the FIR registered at Lodhi Colony police station, a private event management company had approached the South District Police seeking permission to organise the event at the stadium. The event was scheduled to take place between 4.30 am and 10.30 am on October 11, with an expected participation of 1,500 to 2,000 people.However, the police rejected the application on October 10, citing the prevailing law-and-order situation and heightened security arrangements across Delhi following protest calls by certain groups.Despite the denial of a No Objection Certificate (NOC), the organisers allegedly went ahead with the event at around 5 am on October 11, drawing approximately 1,500 to 2,000 participants, as indicated in their original permission application.The FIR states that Delhi was on high alert at the time in anticipation of protests, with police personnel deployed at several locations to maintain law and order. The Lodhi Colony area was also under heightened security surveillance.The complaint further alleges that the gathering violated a prohibitory order issued by the assistant commissioner of police (ACP), which barred the assembly of five or more people in the area. The restrictions were imposed in view of security requirements at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium and the adjoining CGO Complex, which houses several key government offices and agencies.Police have also alleged that the event led to the obstruction of roads and public thoroughfares surrounding the stadium, disrupting vehicular movement and inconveniencing commuters.The organisers have additionally been accused of allowing participants to run on roads designated for vehicular traffic, allegedly endangering lives through negligent conduct.The FIR has been registered under four provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS): Sections 223 (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant), 285 (danger or obstruction in a public way), 125 (act endangering the life or personal safety of others) and 292 (punishment for public nuisance).
Article Summary: Delhi Police has registered an FIR against the organisers of a large-scale running event held at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on October 11. The event was allegedly in violation of a police order denying permission for the gathering. Delhi was on high alert at the time in anticipation of protests, with police personnel deployed at several locations.

Article Title: Gujarat couple killed as bus carrying Jain pilgrims overturns in Jharkhand’s Giridih
Article Text:
Fifty Jain pilgrims were travelling to Jamshedpur for their return journey to Gujarat in a convoy of 10 vehicles after completing their pilgrimage at Sammed Shikharji on Parasnath Hill in Giridih

Bokaro:





A couple from Gujarat was killed, and 12 others were injured after a bus carrying Jain pilgrims overturned in Giridih late on Sunday. The deceased were identified as Babulal Vanshraj (56) and his wife Badami Devi (49), both residents of Surat.Police said a group of 50 pilgrims from Surat was travelling to Jamshedpur in a convoy of 10 vehicles for their return journey after completing their pilgrimage at Sammed Shikharji on Parasnath Hill in Giridih. The bus was a part of the convoy.Police said the bus rammed a roadside tree and overturned on the other side of the road after its driver lost control of the wheels around 10:30 pm. Many passengers got trapped inside the vehicle and had to be rescued.Dumri sub-divisional police officer Abid Khan, with teams from Madhuban and Pirtand police stations, reached the spot and rescued the passengers from the bus with the help of locals. The injured were taken to Pirtand community health centre. Doctors said two passengers sustained serious injuries and were referred to a higher medical facility for specialised treatment.“We heard a sound and everything turned upside down. People were crying for help, and some passengers were bleeding. Villagers and police personnel helped pull us out and rushed us to hospital. We are still in a state of shock,” an injured passenger said.Police took custody of the bodies and initiated legal formalities. An investigation is underway to determine the cause of the accident. “All the injured were shifted to hospital for treatment,” Khan said.
Article Summary: 50 pilgrims from Surat were travelling to Jamshedpur in a convoy of 10 vehicles. Bus rammed a roadside tree and overturned on the other side of the road. The deceased were identified as Babulal Vanshraj (56) and his wife Badami Devi (49)

Article Title: Over 94 ghats readied; divers, cops deployed for Kartik Purnima
Article Text:
Around 385 sanitation workers have been engaged in the cleaning drive

Patna

:





More than 94 ghats along Ganga river in Patna have been prepared for the expected rush of devotees taking a holy dip on Tuesday on Kartik Purnima. The Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC) has completed cleaning, barricading and other arrangements, while the district administration has deployed magistrates, police personnel, divers, river patrol teams and disaster response forces to ensure devotees’ safety.Around 385 sanitation workers have been engaged in the cleaning drive. Puja materials and other waste left behind after Chhath have been removed, and bathing areas cleared to facilitate the movement of devotees. Temporary bathing ponds have also been constructed at LCT Ghat, Rajapur Pul Ghat, Pehalwan Ghat and Abdul Rahmanpur Ghat as alternative bathing facilities.The district administration has put river safety measures in place, deploying NDRF and SDRF teams, motorboats, river patrol teams and divers at major bathing locations. Rescue teams have been directed to remain mobile and respond promptly to emergencies. The administration has also prohibited the unauthorised operation of motorboats and other boats in the river.Magistrates and police personnel have been deployed at major ghats, while temporary control rooms have been set up at crowded locations to manage the rush of devotees and coordinate emergency responses.Ambulances, medical personnel and paramedics have been stationed at major ghats to handle emergencies.The civil surgeon has been directed to ensure round-the-clock emergency medical services at PMCH, NMCH, Guru Gobind Singh Hospital in Patna City and other major hospitals.Special traffic arrangements have also been made to ensure smooth movement of devotees and commuters. Sub-divisional officers and sub-divisional police officers have been instructed to maintain law and order and ensure adequate safety arrangements in their respective jurisdictions.Patna district magistrate Kundan Kumar and senior superintendent of police Kartikeya K Sharma have directed all magistrates and police personnel deployed for the occasion to report at their designated locations on time and remain alert throughout their duty.The administration has appealed to devotees to follow instructions issued by police and magistrates, remain within barricaded bathing areas and avoid ghats declared dangerous or unsuitable for bathing. They have also been advised to exercise caution while entering the river and follow safety protocols.
Article Summary: More than 94 ghats along Ganga river in Patna have been prepared for the expected rush of devotees. Puja materials and other waste left behind after Chhath have been removed. Temporary bathing ponds have also been constructed at LCT Ghat, Rajapur Pul Ghat and Pehalwan Ghat.

Article Title: Fire breaks out at Navi Mumbai oil warehouse, spreads to two buildings
Article Text:
Firefighters were deployed to the scene upon receiving the alert

(With Agency Inputs)





MUMBAI: A major fire broke out at an oil warehouse in the Mefco Market area of Turbhe in Navi Mumbai, prompting an emergency response from local fire brigade teams. Firefighters rushed to the spot after receiving an alert and are currently working to bring the blaze under control.According to an eyewitness, Rakesh, the fire spread beyond the warehouse and engulfed adjoining structures."Right now, it has caught in two," Rakesh told reporters at the scene, indicating that two buildings had been engulfed by the fire.Further details are awaited.In a separate incident earlier this month, a firefighter sustained burn injuries while trying to douse a fire at a garage-cum-warehouse in the Kalamboli steel market, which triggered a massive explosion.Deputy Fire Officer Manish Brahmankar said the incident occurred around 10.30pm on Saturday night.He said the fire control room received a call reporting that a shop had caught fire, following which a fire crew was immediately dispatched to the spot. However, upon reaching the location, the team found that the blaze had originated in a garage-cum-warehouse."Around 10:30 PM, our control room received a call reporting that a shop had caught fire.We immediately dispatched a fire crew to the scene. Upon arrival, we discovered that the fire was not in a shop, but rather in a garage and a godown," he said.The deputy fire officer said a sudden explosion occurred due to several drums of chemicals stored inside the warehouse."We had no information regarding what chemicals were stored inside. Suddenly, a massive explosion occurred; we later identified the cause as several drums of thinner that were kept inside," he said.A firefighter sustained 5-6 per cent burn injuries while attempting to douse the blaze and was admitted to a hospital for treatment. The warehouse owner is currently missing, while officials are yet to ascertain the cause of the fire."One of our firefighters was injured in the blast, sustaining 5-6 per cent burn injuries, and has been hospitalised. The owner of the premises is currently missing, and a report has been filed at the police station. Preliminary inspection has not yet revealed the cause of the fire," he said.
Article Summary: Fire broke out at an oil warehouse in the Mefco Market area of Turbhe in Navi Mumbai. Firefighters rushed to the spot after receiving an alert and are currently working to bring the blaze under control. A firefighter sustained 5-6 per cent burn injuries while attempting to douse the blaze and was admitted to a hospital.

Article Title: ​​10,767km, 3 states later, rare vulture makes first recorded halt in Maharashtra's Latur
Article Text:
Critically endangered the Indian vulture seen in Ausa taluka of Latur district-

More than just a rare sighting





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: A seven-year-old female Indian vulture, released into the wild at Melghat Tiger Reserve, made a halt in Latur’s Ausa taluka after clocking 10,767 km, marking the first recorded sighting of the critically endangered species in the district.It had flown thousands of kilometres across three states, crossed forests and open landscapes and even ventured into Karnataka. Then, on Nov 18, the vulture stopped in Latur.The bird is no anonymous visitor. A yellow ring on its left leg carries the tag F14. A blue one on its right reads M99. A tracking device on its back has allowed Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) to follow its remarkable journey.The vulture was bred at BNHS’s vulture breeding centre at Pinjore in Haryana. It was later released in the Somthana forest range of Melghat along with 15 other Indian vultures.Its brief Latur stop created excitement among local birders. Wildlife enthusiast Abhijit Rasal alerted Latur-based wildlife lover Dhananjay Gutte on the night of Nov 18. Before dawn, Gutte, deputy conservator of forests (Social Forestry) Amitraj Jadhav and local birder Datta Ambekar headed to the roosting site.They reached at 5.30 am and waited.“After spending some time, we spotted the vulture perched on a tree. We photographed and videographed it. The bird appeared healthy and was moving naturally in the wild,” Gutte said.The visitor did not stay for long. At 8.40 am, it took off again. It later reached Murbad taluka in Thane district.From Melghat to MP, Karnataka and back. The Latur halt is only one chapter in F14/M99’s long journey.Abhijeet Das, project biologist with BNHS’s Vulture Project Maharashtra, said the bird initially remained close to its release site in Melghat. “After its release, F14/M99 stayed near the site, learning to forage and building its flight muscles. It dispersed from the release site on May 28, crossing Maharashtra and reaching Madhya Pradesh. It used several landscapes known to support wild vulture populations,” Das said.Then came an observation that conservationists consider particularly significant. On Sept 18, F14/M99 was spotted near Halali dam in Madhya Pradesh. It was roosting with wild vultures. More importantly, it had a full crop, indicating it had fed successfully.“This provides the first evidence that the released birds are capable of independent foraging and integrating with the wild population,” Das said.For a bird bred in captivity and released into the wild, those two things matter enormously: finding its own food and finding its place among wild vultures.Das said the traveller returned to Maharashtra on Nov 13.“The bird entered Maharashtra again on Nov 13, crossing Akot and Malkapur and reaching Nashik, Thane and Pune. It then travelled south to near Vijayapura in Karnataka. It returned to Maharashtra on Nov 18, taking a route through Latur, and reached Thane again on Nov 20,” he said.The Indian vulture (Gyps indicus) is listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List. The species performs one of nature’s least glamorous but most vital jobs. Vultures rapidly dispose of animal carcasses, helping keep the landscape clean and limiting opportunities for disease to spread.India once had vast populations of vultures. Their numbers crashed dramatically, with experts largely linking the decline to the veterinary use of diclofenac. That makes every successfully released bird important.And every sign that a captive-bred vulture can survive, feed and move naturally in the wild adds another piece to the conservation puzzle.For Gutte, however, F14/M99’s journey has also put Latur on the vulture map. He said the district’s first recorded sighting was encouraging for conservation and raised hopes that its landscape could offer suitable habitat for vultures.F14/M99, meanwhile, has already moved on. Its Latur visit lasted barely a morning. But after 10,767 km in the wild, one night’s halt was enough to leave behind a first for the district.
Article Summary: A seven-year-old female Indian vulture, released into the wild at Melghat Tiger Reserve, made a halt in Latur’s Ausa taluka. It had flown thousands of kilometres across three states, crossed forests and open landscapes and even ventured into Karnataka. A tracking device on its back has allowed Bombay Natural History Society to follow its remarkable journey.

Article Title: Ladki Bahin has strained Maharashtra finances, but can’t step back from it: Narhari Zirwal
Article Text:
The programme, launched ahead of the 2024 assembly elections, provides eligible women Rs 1,500 a month.

Ladkya Bahini





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Food and drug administration minister Narhari Zirwal on Saturday acknowledged that the Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin scheme has put Maharashtra govt in a difficult financial position, with drought now adding to the strain on the state’s finances.Speaking at a public event in Loha during a tour of Nanded district , Zirwal said govt could not step back from the flagship welfare scheme despite the burden it had created. “Nobody told us before the election to launch the scheme, but we made many(beloved sisters). Now, we cannot distance ourselves from them,” Zirwal said.He described the state’s financial position as “strained” because of the scheme. “To add to it, we now have a drought,” he said.His remarks are significant as they amount to a rare acknowledgement from within the state cabinet of the fiscal pressure created by the Ladki Bahin scheme. The programme, launched ahead of the 2024 assembly elections, provides eligible women Rs 1,500 a month.Zirwal said the drought would require substantial additional spending, particularly if the water crisis worsens. “The 1972 drought caused a shortage of food.This time, we have a water shortage. We may even have to arrange water through planes or trains, and such measures will require huge funds,” he said.The NCP politician, however, said govt would ensure there was no shortage of resources in tackling the drought.His remarks come days after deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde said on Nov 9 that govt would take a decision at an appropriate time on increasing the monthly Ladki Bahin assistance from Rs 1,500 to Rs 2,100. Shinde and chief minister Devendra Fadnavis have repeatedly maintained that the scheme will continue.Zirwal also raised eyebrows with a separate remark that “NCP’s clock is not keeping accurate time”, referring to the party’s election symbol. He later sought to clarify the remark. “When Ajit Dada was alive, all public functions started on time because he was very punctual. Now, programmes sometimes get delayed. My comment was made only in that context,” he said.
Article Summary: Food and drug administration minister Narhari Zirwal acknowledged that the Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin scheme has put Maharashtra govt in a difficult financial position. He described the state’s financial position as ‘strained’ because of the scheme. The programme provides eligible women Rs 1,500 a month.

Article Title: Latur police register 8 cases over noise pollution violations, seize sound systems worth Rs 8.5 lakh
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: Latur police have registered cases against eight people for violating prescribed noise pollution limits during processions held to mark Hazrat Tipu Sultan birth anniversary on Friday.Police also seized three vehicles fitted with high-powered sound systems worth an estimated Rs 8.5 lakh after detecting unauthorised modifications.Of the eight cases, four were registered at MIDC police station, three at Vivekanand Chowk police station, and one at Shivajinagar police station, said Latur superintendent of police Amol Tambe.Sub-divisional police officer (SDPO) Sameersinh Salve said police teams used sound-level measuring devices to monitor noise during the processions. They recorded sound intensity and collected readings to establish violations before initiating legal action against those found using loudspeakers and sound systems beyond permissible limits.In a separate action, MIDC police seized three vehicles fitted with high-capacity sound systems after detecting unauthorised modifications. The equipment installed in the vehicles is estimated to be worth Rs 8.5 lakh.Proposals are being sent to the Regional Transport Office (RTO) for further penal and legal action against the vehicle owners.SP Tambe said police have consistently been creating awareness about the harmful effects of noise pollution and urging organisers to adhere to prescribed limits during religious, social, and public events.“Police have been appealing to mandals, organisers, and citizens through peace committee meetings and social media campaigns to ensure that noise pollution norms are followed during processions and public celebrations. While several mandals have responded positively, strict legal action will be taken against those who continue to violate the prescribed limits despite repeated appeals. There will be no compromise on noise pollution,” Tambe said.He added that excessive noise adversely affects senior citizens, infants, pregnant women, and patients, besides disturbing the daily lives of other residents.Police have equipped several stations in the district with sound-measuring devices to monitor noise levels during major festivals, anniversaries, and public gatherings. Tambe appealed to citizens and event organisers to exercise social responsibility and cooperate with the police in keeping Latur free from noise pollution.
Article Summary: Latur police have registered cases against eight people for violating noise pollution limits during processions held to mark Hazrat Tipu Sultan birth anniversary. Police also seized three vehicles fitted with high-powered sound systems worth an estimated Rs 8.5 lakh after detecting unauthorised modifications.

Article Title: Latur police book 80 in district-wide illegal liquor crackdown
Article Text: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:The Latur police registered 80 cases and initiated action against 80 people during a district-wide crackdown on the illegal liquor trade on Thursday. The special drive was conducted simultaneously across all 23 police station jurisdictions in the district on November 20.Police seized liquor and other materials collectively valued at Rs 3.81 lakh during the operation.Latur superintendent of police Amol Tambe said the drive involved 152 police personnel, including 25 officers and 127 constables and other personnel. Teams were deployed across the district to identify and raid locations where illegal liquor was being sold.Tambe said that he had directed police officials to sustain action against illegal activities, including the sale of illicit liquor, gambling and matka operations.Apart from registering cases, the police are also initiating preventive action against those involved in such activities. The offenders are required to execute legal bonds undertaking not to repeat the offences. Those found violating these conditions and resuming illegal activities will face further stringent legal action.The police said the objective was not merely to book offenders but also to deter them from returning to illegal activities and prevent the recurrence of such businesses.Similar special drives will continue across the district to curb illegal activities and maintain law and order, police said.
Article Summary: The Latur police registered 80 cases and initiated action against 80 people during a district-wide crackdown on the illegal liquor trade on Thursday. The special drive was conducted simultaneously across all 23 police station jurisdictions in the district on November 20. Police seized liquor and other materials collectively valued at Rs 3.81 lakh during the operation.
